page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.n1.medium is an entry-tier x86_64 cloud server instance powered by an Intel Xeon 8163 processor clocked at 2.5 GHz. The configuration allocates 2 virtual CPUs across a single physical core with hyperthreading enabled. It includes 4.0 GB of system memory, yielding a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. The instance contains no bundled local storage, requiring network-attached storage for persistent disk needs, and includes zero hardware accelerators and no complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark evaluations place performance levels in the lower percentiles across compute and memory subsystems. In stress-ng testing, single-core throughput ranks in the lower 25 percent, while multi-core metrics fall into the bottom 10 percent. Geekbench results record weak single-core and poor multi-core scoring, with software compilation and image processing similarly ranking in the lowest decile. PassMark testing mirrors these findings, showing poor marks for overall CPU capability, memory processing, and database operations. Network-adjacent workloads, including static web serving throughput and Redis operations, also register in the lower tiers.

The instance provides a compact compute footprint with dedicated hyperthreaded execution on an older-generation architecture. While it lacks local high-speed storage and advanced AVX-512 VNNI or matrix acceleration instructions, it retains support for baseline AVX-512F, AES, and BMI2 instruction sets. Given its lower throughput relative to modern dense hardware, this tier provides cost efficiency for non-intensive utility workloads, internal development and testing nodes, simple automation scripts, and low-traffic staging environments.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.n1.medium is an entry-level x86_64 instance configured with 2 vCPUs from a single physical core of an Intel Xeon 8163 processor running at 2.5 GHz. It is equipped with 4.0 GB of RAM, establishing a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio, and includes neither integrated local storage nor hardware acceleration GPUs. Performance benchmarks place the instance primarily within the lower quartile and bottom decile across single-core and multi-core evaluations, including stress-ng, Geekbench, and PassMark suites. Memory bandwidth and operations such as compression, database tasks, and static web serving also demonstrate modest throughput. Without local NVMe disks or included public IPv4 addresses, storage must be attached over the network. This resource profile offers cost-effective execution for non-critical, lightweight workloads including low-volume testing, administrative automation, staging servers, and background utilities that do not demand extensive compute capacity or high I/O throughput.
